dedupe_keys.name: food supply chain digital twin for cyber range exercises jamk finland

description: This case study describes a digital twin of a food supply chain that JAMK University of Applied Sciences in Finland built so that organisations can rehearse cyber attacks on food supply. Each part of the chain, from ingredients to products, runs as a Node.js service on the university's Realistic Global Cyber Environment cyber range, and the flow of goods is simulated with an apparatus model and message queues. The twin was used in a live cyber exercise, where the authors judged the approach scalable and realistic enough; they note that it is tied to one platform and needs feedback from more exercises. The article is free to read and download as open access under CC BY 4.0 in Applied Sciences (2023). Coverage is a generic food supply chain modelled for Finnish cyber exercises, not a specific company. Caveats: the facts here come from the article abstract; the twin runs only inside the RGCE cyber range and no code is stated as available. Simulation uses: a testbed for cyber attack scenarios on food production and logistics, and a template for coupling supply chain flows to IT systems in exercises. Related records: the Global Food Twin (platform-global-food-twin) is a global, physical-flow digital twin of the food system.
